text:
Anya: heads-up — saw a couple customer regressions when our eviction moved a prefix mid-handoff. Read-after-write failures for a few seconds :grimacing:
Mike: ugh. can you paste the log snippet?
Anya: here —
```
Anya 17:18:12 Handoff started prefix=tenant/abc shard=3 -> 4
Anya 17:18:12 Lease bumped id=lk-42 ttl=30s
Anya 17:18:13 Evict candidate prefix=tenant/abc slab=hot
Anya 17:18:14 Handoff commit ack missing for 2s -> client read misses
```
Sam: quick q — is the handoff using the same lease/ownership token or a separate ephemeral handshake?
Anya: ephemeral. we create a temporary lease on target + release on source after commit ack. Seems the release happened while some in-flight KV writes still landed on source.
Julie: sounds like a race: writes replayed to source after we told clients to read from target.
Anya: exactly. currently client routing switches on lease acquisition without waiting for an explicit finalization signal from the sequencer.
Mike: options I see: 1) make handoff two-phase commit (explicit finalize ack) 2) extend grace TTL on source after lease transfer 3) piggyback in-flight write markers / sequence numbers and drain in-flight queue
Sam: 1) is safest but expensive and painful for scaling; adds global sync.
Julie: 2) seems pragmatic — add a configurable grace window per prefix, e.g., 500ms-5s depending on workload. Also emit metric when grace used.
Anya: agree on metrics. we currently have per-prefix lease_ttl and renew, but no graceful-release interval. Could add `release_grace_ms` in the handshake response.
Mike: small API change: handshake response -> {lease_id, lease_ttl_ms, release_grace_ms}. Clients would keep reading from both source+target during grace with precedence to target.
Sam: reading both adds extra load; but we can prefer target and fallback to source if miss. cheaper than 2PC.
Julie: we should also consider pinned prefixes and shared pool semantics. if a prefix is pinned, release_grace_ms should be ignored (don't evict). If in shared pool then grace might be shorter.
Anya: good point. policy matrix: pinned -> no move; shared-hot -> short grace + instrumentation; shared-cold -> longer grace to avoid churn storms.
Mike: what about the correctness invariant? we need to guarantee monotonic reads post-transition. If we allow fallback reads to source, clients might read stale data unless we ensure sequencing.
Sam: we can attach a per-write sequence number (incrementing per-prefix) and return the last-seen seq in handshake. During grace, target can compare seq and apply missing entries from source or reject reads until seq catches up. That avoids full 2PC but needs minimal metadata.
Anya: love that. implementation sketch: handshake returns last_seq_target; source exposes tail seq; client read includes seen_seq; if read from target and seq < seen_seq -> proxy fetches from source or stalls for up to grace window.
Julie: we should also add an instrumentation event when proxy had to fetch fallbacks, plus a tracer span for the handoff boundary.
infra-bot: deploy-checklist: add feature-flag `handoff_grace` + metrics `handoff_fallback_count` and `handoff_long_tail_ms`.
Mike: next debate: should grace default to 0.5s or 2s? I lean 500ms for hot prefixes to keep churn low, 2s for cold.
Sam: default 500ms and make it adaptive: if we detect high write qps during move, extend grace automatically up to 5s.
Anya: action items: 1) Mike draft handshake payload change + client read semantics (PR) 2) Sam spike seq-based fallback proof-of-concept 3) Julie add metrics/tracing + prod dashboard 4) Feature flag rollout plan (infra-bot)
Julie: I'll own metrics + dashboard.
Mike: I'll start the PR for handshake schema.
Sam: taking the spike. will report perf numbers.
Anya: thanks — will collect customer repros to validate. tagging this with follow-up in the RFC thread. :thumbsup:
